title: Potato Dynamics Upgrade — Frobenius Closure, Door Transversality and Bifurcation Discipline
status: archive-generated mathematical contribution extending Potato Dynamics 2.0; differential geometry and dynamical-systems structure adapted to the project grammar
abstract: Potato Dynamics already distinguishes ordinary time flow F from structural/Axis flow A and uses their Lie bracket to test commutation. This upgrade asks a stronger question: even when F and A do not commute, do they still generate a closed two-dimensional dynamical surface, or does their interaction create genuinely new directions that the current state description omits? Using the Frobenius involutivity criterion, the model distinguishes strict commutation, noncommuting-but-closed two-flow dynamics, and non-closure requiring additional state directions. Door events are sharpened by distinguishing transverse crossings, grazing contacts and true bifurcations, preventing every threshold event from receiving the same transition label.

axis_time_distribution.distribution: D_x=span{F(x),A(x)} wherever F and A are linearly independent.
axis_time_distribution.strict_commutation: [F,A]=0; under regularity assumptions the local flows commute.
axis_time_distribution.frobenius_consequence: For a smooth constant-rank involutive distribution, local integral surfaces exist whose tangent planes are D. Axis and time may fail to commute yet remain closed inside a two-dimensional leaf.
axis_time_distribution.nonclosure: If [F,A] has a component outside span{F,A}, repeated time/Axis operations generate a direction omitted by the declared two-flow state description.

closure_defect.definition: C_perp(x)=||(I-P_D)[F,A](x)||_g, with a declared metric/inner product g and projection P_D onto span{F,A}.
closure_defect.meaning: C_perp=0 is a local involutivity diagnostic; nonzero values measure omitted-direction generation.
closure_defect.warning: Magnitude depends on coordinates, metric and scaling, so cross-system comparisons require normalization.

door_event_geometry.transverse_crossing: dh_x(F)!=0 at the event; the trajectory crosses the guard robustly to first order.
door_event_geometry.grazing: dh_x(F)=0 at h=0; first-order transversality fails and event timing can become highly sensitive.
door_event_geometry.axis_crossing: Use dh_x(A) for the structural flow; a guard can be transverse for one flow and tangent for the other.

bifurcation_discipline.principle: A threshold crossing, hybrid reset and bifurcation are distinct mathematical objects.
comparators: pitchfork: xdot=mu x-x^3 when symmetry supports it
Hopf: a conjugate eigenvalue pair crosses the imaginary axis with the required nondegeneracy
bifurcation_discipline.rule: Do not assign a named bifurcation merely because the visual story resembles it; derive the equilibrium, Jacobian and theorem conditions.

advancement_gates.axis: Evaluate rank and involutivity before treating Axis as a coherent second flow.
advancement_gates.door: Verify transversality or explicitly model grazing before assigning robust event statistics.
advancement_gates.bifurcation: Derive local normal-form conditions before naming the Door's bifurcation type.
advancement_gates.state_space: If C_perp is systematically nonzero, enlarge the model rather than hiding the missing direction.

failure_conditions: Axis/time are called a closed two-coordinate system while their bracket generates omitted directions.
A grazing contact is treated as a robust crossing without sensitivity analysis.
A normal-form name is assigned without checking linearization/nondegeneracy/symmetry.
A threshold is called universal even though Axis transport substantially changes the guard.
